content_voiceover: This diagram maps out the domain structure of pre-pro-VWF and it's loaded with board-relevant, testable detail. The precursor is cleaved by signal peptidase to remove the signal peptide, then furin cleaves between the propeptide and the mature protein at the D prime-D3 boundary, releasing the VWF propeptide, which is actually required for proper multimer assembly and is co-secreted alongside mature VWF. The mature VWF subunit contains, from N to C terminus, the D prime and D3 domains which bind factor VIII, the A1 domain which binds platelet GPIb-alpha, mediating platelet adhesion under high shear, the A2 domain which contains the ADAMTS13 cleavage site, the enzyme that trims ultra-large multimers, deficiency of which causes TTP, the A3 domain which binds subendothelial collagen, and the C1 and C2 domains which contain the RGD sequence binding platelet GPIIb-IIIa. Multimerization occurs through disulfide bonds at the N-terminal D prime-D3 region, while dimerization occurs through the C-terminal CK, or cystine knot, domain. This structure-function map explains why different mutation locations produce different VWD subtypes, a mutation in A1 affects GPIb binding and gives type two M, a mutation in A2 near the ADAMTS13 site increases susceptibility to cleavage and gives type two A, and a mutation in D prime-D3 impairs factor VIII binding and gives type two N.
keypoints: A1 domain binds GPIbα (shear-dependent platelet adhesion)
A2 domain has the ADAMTS13 cleavage site (deficiency -> TTP)
A3 domain binds collagen; D'-D3 binds factor VIII
C1/C2 domains bind GPIIb/IIIa via an RGD motif
N-terminal D'-D3 = multimerization; C-terminal CK = dimerization
keypoint_voiceover: Know the VWF domain map. A1 binds platelet GPIb-alpha for shear-dependent adhesion, A2 contains the ADAMTS13 cleavage site, whose deficiency causes TTP, A3 binds subendothelial collagen, and D prime-D3 binds factor VIII. The C1 and C2 domains bind GPIIb-IIIa through an RGD motif. Multimerization happens at the N-terminal D prime-D3 region while dimerization happens through the C-terminal CK domain, and mutations in these specific domains map directly onto the different VWD type two subtypes.
